messages:
Sarah Park: Quick RFC follow-up — I opened a lightweight proposal for fragmented artifact updates for air-gapped/on‑prem nodes. Goal: allow small patch deltas that can be stitched locally to avoid full bundle transfers. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/rfcs/pulls/842
Mike Chen: Nice. Is this the approach where the operator applies 'fragments' with a manifest-level checksum chain? sounds similar to talked about but smaller scope.
Sarah Park: Yep. Manifest contains fragment ranges + cumulative hash. Operator validates chain and applies in-order. We still keep sealed bundle fallback for full restore.
Jenny O'Neil: How do we handle partial failures mid-apply? operator idempotency is key.
Sarah Park: Good point — proposal suggests an apply journal on the node and a compacted tombstone list. If fragment N fails, operator retries and verifies checksum; we can mark fragment as corrupt and fetch from a different media.
Ops Bot: deploy-bot: PR 842 created by sarah — review requested: @Mike Chen @Nate Rivera :eyes: 
Nate Rivera: I'm worried about reordering from physical media transfer (USB sticks). We should include sequence numbers and a simple vector of applied fragments so operator can detect holes.
Lisa Gomez: Can we surface an admin-level dry-run mode? admin runs: `operator apply --source /mnt/usb --dry-run` to validate checksums without applying.
Mike Chen: I'm also thinking about GC. If we keep fragments around, space could blow. Proposal mentions TTL and compaction policy tied to successful activation. Agree?
Sarah Park: Yes TTL + op-triggered compaction after activation + periodic GC. We'll also sign fragments; signature granularity can be per-fragment or per-bundle. Tradeoff table in PR.
Jenny O'Neil: Signing per-fragment increases metadata overhead but helps partial trust models. Might be required for some gov customers.
Nate Rivera: On verification speed — doing SHA256 per-fragment on low-powered appliances could be slow. Consider BLAKE3 option in manifest to speed verifies.
Sarah Park: Good call. I added BLAKE3 as opt-in in the spec. Fallback to SHA256 for legacy validators.
Lisa Gomez: How do rollbacks work if fragment apply partially succeeds? do we keep reverse fragments?
Sarah Park: Operator will record each activation step; rollback uses snapshot + reverse-apply script included in bundle fragments. We avoid reverse fragments for large changes and instead recommend a fast full-bundle fallback for safety.
Mike Chen: Operational UX: would love an operator endpoint `/apply/status` returning JSON summary for remote support. That helps troubleshooting when customers are air-gapped.
Sarah Park: Agree, adding an unobtrusive read-only status endpoint with activation ledger. No sensitive data returned.
Jenny O'Neil: Can we add a short example of the manifest format in the RFC? a tiny example helps adoption.
Sarah Park: Added example in PR:
```
manifest:
  version: 1
  algo: blake3
  fragments:
    - seq: 1
      size: 12MB
      hash: "b3..."
    - seq: 2
      size: 4MB
      hash: "b8..."
  signature: "sig-v1"
```
Nate Rivera: Looks reasonable. One last ask: include operator metrics (apply_duration, verify_errors, gc_runs) so we can alert on stuck applies.
Sarah Park: Added metrics section. Thanks all — can reviewers please +1 or leave explicit objections on PR 842 by EOD Thursday? Otherwise I'll merge and start a small pilot with infra-team next week. :rocket:
